doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Basie's sense of tempo and reverence for him
summary: The Neal Hefti 'Li'l Darling' tempo story, musicians' reverence for Basie versus Ellington and Goodman, Joe calling him Mr. Basie, and Nestico arrangements.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: He always will be. Because he was the key. Clark Terry this morning, it’s often been written that the real secret to Bill Basie was that he always knew the right tempo for a tune. And Clark told a story of “L’il Darling?”
Yeah, when Neal Hefti brought it in.

When Neal Hefti brought it in and said, “here’s the tempo.” And Basie says, “no, this is the tempo.” And they played it that way and it was a huge hit. And as Clark says, if they’d played it with Hefti’s speed, it would have been another “who heard of it?”
Yes, it would have been gone long ago.

But he had that, and that — I mean he had sort of a mystic — I mean all the people I’ve ever met who played in the band, speak of him with reverence. And I don’t know, that’s not true, even Ellington, who is a great one, there are people who played with Ellington who don’t speak highly of him. And certainly there are people who played with Benny Goodman who don’t speak highly of him. In fact it’s hard to find one who does.
Yes. He’s quite a legend with that.
Benny Goodman stories are wonderful. They’re all very funny stories of things he did.
Yes. But Basie had something, that you know your husband still reveres him.
Oh, absolutely. He still calls him Mr. Basie. Always calls him Mr. Basie.

A couple of the players have mentioned — that we’ve seen — that they had never played in any other bands that could swing at a soft and slow tempo like that. That’s one of the hardest things for bands to do, is to be soft and slow but still be happening.
All those wonderful Nestico arrangements that nobody plays them like the Basie band, all of those, “Queen Bee” and lovely things that he arranged. Terrific.

Well there’s a whole library of stuff that nobody plays like Basie. Even the current Basie band doesn’t play it as well as they were. Although the new Basie band is not all that bad. © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
